input_signals.name: PERSISTENT_RND_STABLE_ACCRUALS
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent R&D intensity predicts higher returns when accrual quality is stable rather than noisy.
input_signals.reasoning: Sustained R&D programs are more likely to represent deliberate intangible capital formation than one-off spending spikes. Low volatility in accruals helps distinguish firms with consistent underlying economics from firms where intangible spending coincides with unstable accounting measurement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( xrd, sale ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RND_ACCEL_CASH_FUNDED
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(xrd, sale))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), ADD(at, ABS(SUB(ib, oancf))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D acceleration is most return-relevant when it is supported by cash-generating operations rather than by accrual-driven reported earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts away from a static R&D-intensity plus accrual double sort by focusing on a change in intangible investment intensity and whether the firm has cash capacity to absorb it. Adding back R&D to operating cash flow approximates pre-R&D cash profitability, while the accrual gap in the denominator penalizes earnings quality noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( xrd, sale ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), add( at, abs( sub( ib, oancf ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RND_MOAT_CASH_VERIFIED
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ib), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with industry-relative gross-margin strength earn higher returns when that apparent intangible moat is verified by persistent cash earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the rejected signed revenue-growth and receivables-accrual structure with a product-market validation mechanism. Industry-adjusted gross margins identify potentially productive innovation, while the smoothed R&D-adjusted cash-versus-earnings wedge filters out cases where the apparent moat is mainly accounting-supported.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( mul( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ) ) ) ), rank( ma( ratio( sub( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), ib ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CAPITALIZED_INTAN_CASH_DIVERGENCE
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ib), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms increasing recognized intangible assets underperform when R&D-adjusted cash verification is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: Recognized intangible growth can reflect acquisitions, capitalization, or accounting estimates whose value is hard to validate. If the cash-versus-earnings wedge worsens at the same time, the intangible build is more likely to represent accounting opacity than productive investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), ib ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GOODWILL_GROWTH_ACCRUAL_NONARTICULATION
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(gdwl, at), 1)), RANK(ABS(SUB(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at), RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with growing goodwill underperform when cash-flow-based working-capital accruals and balance-sheet working-capital accruals diverge sharply.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual-disagreement leg is corrected by adding back depreciation to the cash-flow accrual measure, making it comparable to a balance-sheet working-capital accrual measure. Pairing this with continuous goodwill growth targets acquisition-related accounting non-articulation rather than a generic recognized-intangibles level.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( gdwl, at ), 1 ) ), rank( abs( sub( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), dp ), at ), ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RND_MOAT_EXPANSION_CASH_VERIFIED
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), TREND(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)), 3))), RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ib), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms earn higher returns when industry-relative gross margins are improving and the improvement is supported by R&D-adjusted cash earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than reusing a static margin moat, this targets firms where innovation appears to be expanding pricing power. The cash-verification leg filters out cases where apparent margin improvement is accompanied by accrual-supported earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( mul( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), trend( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ) ), 3 ) ) ), rank( ma( ratio( sub( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), ib ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CAPITALIZED_RND_SUBSTITUTION_ACCRUAL
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when recognized intangible assets rise relative to expensed R&D intensity while reported earnings are accrual-supported.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces another R&D-backlog stability variant with a substitution mechanism: the firm appears to be shifting from internally expensed innovation toward capitalized or acquired intangible balances. That shift is most concerning when earnings simultaneously exceed operating cash flow, suggesting accounting presentation rather than productive intangible investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( delta( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), 1 ), delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CAPITALIZED_INTAN_PRODUCTIVITY_TRAP
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1)), MUL(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms increasing recognized intangible assets underperform when asset productivity is declining and reported earnings exceed operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the already-tested capitalized-versus-R&D substitution leg and focuses on whether a growing intangible asset base is producing revenue efficiency. If sales-to-assets is deteriorating while earnings remain accrual-supported, the recognized intangible build is less likely to represent productive investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( rank( neg( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )
